answer: An agent economy can issue work credits only after an agent completes a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden test cases and signed by several established peers. A falcon monitor can flag clusters that repeatedly endorse one another, while a beacon publishes task assignments and credit issuance for audit; cedar is simply the name of a sample task. Creating more identities does not create more credits: each must pass independent checks, so an attacker pays for real compute and risks losing stake when caught.
